facts.statement: Lukousaurus is an extinct archosauromorph known from a small snout with distinctive lacrimal horns found in Yunnan, China.
facts.quote: Lukousaurus is an extinct genus of archosauromorph based on most of a small snout, displaying distinctive lacrimal horns, found in the Early Jurassic lower Lufeng Formation of Yunnan, China.

facts.statement: Fossils including a partial skull, lower jaws, a tooth, and a humerus were discovered in the late 1930s in Huangchiatien, Yunnan Province.
facts.quote: In the late 1930s, a partial anterior skull and lower jaws, as well as a tooth and humerus were found in the town of Huangchiatien (also called Dahungtien) in Yunnan Province.

facts.statement: The holotype skull was found in strata originally thought to be Triassic but are now known to be Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: The skull was found in the lower Jurassic strata of the Red Beds of the Lufeng Formation, though at the time of its naming in 1940 by Chung Chien Young, the beds were thought to date to the Triassic.

facts.statement: The species name yini honors T. H. Yin, a former deputy director of the Geological Survey of China who worked during the Japanese invasion.
facts.quote: The specific name honors the former deputy Director of the Geological Survey of China, T. H. Yin, who continued work on the survey despite the Japanese invasion.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is housed at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing under the number IVPP 23.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is housed within the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, China under specimen number IVPP 23.

facts.statement: Lukousaurus was originally classified as a theropod dinosaur but later research suggests it may be related to suchian archosaurs.
facts.quote: Lukousaurus was originally tentatively classified as a theropod dinosaur, allied with ceratosaurs or coelurosaurs, though other researchers have reinforced non-dinosaurian affinities, possibly related to suchians.

facts.statement: Lukousaurus has a robust skull for its size, and its teeth were initially thought to be typical of theropods.
facts.quote: Its skull is rather robust for its size, though the teeth were initially described as typically theropodan.

facts.statement: Mickey Mortimer revised her classification of Lukousaurus from a ceratosaur or sphenosuchian to a basal pseudosuchian in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2008, Mickey Mortimer believed that Lukousaurus was either an abelisaurid ceratosaur or a sphenosuchian, but revised her position in 2011 after recovering it as a basal pseudosuchian using a phylogenetic matrix developed by Sterling Nesbitt.

facts.statement: Studies by Knoll et al. (2012) and Irmis (2004) support the view that Lukousaurus is a suchian archosaur rather than a theropod or dinosauromorph.
facts.quote: Knoll et al. (2012) found Lukousaurus to be similar to suchian archosaurs in the anatomy of the antorbital fenestra and Irmis (2004) stated that Lukousaurus wasn't a theropod dinosaur or even a dinosauromorph in general.

facts.statement: Lukousaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 209 to 190 million years ago, in the Hettangian and Sinemurian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 209 a 190 millones de años, en el Hettangiense y en el Sinemuriense.

facts.statement: The time range for Lukousaurus is estimated to be between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Lukousaurus is classified within the suborder Loricata and infraorder Crocodylomorpha.
facts.quote: superordo: Crurotarsi ordo: Pseudosuchia subordo: Loricata infraordo: Crocodylomorpha

facts.statement: While long classified as a coelurosaurian theropod, Irmis (2004) and Knoll et al. (2012) classify Lukousaurus as a basal crocodylomorph.
facts.quote: Aunque clasificado durante mucho tiempo como un terópodo celofisoide, Irmis (2004) y Knoll et al. (2012) lo clasifican como crocodilomorfo basal.

facts.statement: The classification of Lukousaurus remains very uncertain due to the unusual characteristics of its type specimen and referred humerus.
facts.quote: The classification of Lukousaurus is very uncertain due to the strange characteristics of the type specimen and its referred humerus.

rejected.statement: The genus name Lukousaurus honors the Lugou Bridge near Beijing, a symbol of resistance during the Sino-Japanese War.
rejected.quote: The generic name refers to the Lugou Bridge, lit. 'crossroads', near Beijing, where the Sino-Japanese War started and a symbol of the Chinese resistance against Japanese imperialism.
